title: Polynomial-time serialization of a wired formula
statement: Let $\varphi$ be a CNF formula over natural-number variables, and let $wire$ assign a natural-number variable index to each input word and each local index. Suppose that, for every natural number $j$, the unary word of length $wire(x,j)$ is polynomial-time computable as a function of the input word $x$. Then the function that relabels every variable of $\varphi$ using $wire(x,\cdot)$ and serializes the resulting clauses with a leading marker for each clause is polynomial-time computable.
hypotheses_covered: A CNF formula over natural-number variables
A wiring function from an input word and a natural-number index to a natural-number variable index
For every index $j$, the unary encoding of $wire(x,j)$ is polynomial-time computable in $x$
replaced: For every fixed CNF table and every wiring whose unary index is polynomial-time computable at each of the finitely many template variables, the function emitting the serialized fragment of the relabeled table is polynomial-time computable; every literal occurrence pays its variable-index cost, and the formula terminator is deliberately absent from the fragment.
